mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate relative to historical averages compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate for equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25% (as of t-1mo), or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.5% in a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.5% over a 3-month period, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales (HOUST and RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities as corporate revenue expectations fall, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by more than 1% in a month, or Rank IC is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening manufacturing activity that precedes a recession, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO declines in late-cycle expansion, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 2.5%, it signals persistent inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% year-over-year, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high labor market tightness (defined by UNRATE < 5.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5%), a decline in the unemployment rate signals excessive labor demand that may trigger wage inflation and central bank tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE declines in high labor market tightness, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) relative to the previous year indicates strong consumer spending that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS grows year-over-year, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both unemployment rate (UNRATE) and employment growth (PAYEMS) indicate a weakening labor market that reduces consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both UNRATE and PAYEMS decline, or Rank IC is negative over any 3-year rolling window.
